title: A method package for electrophysiological evaluation of reconstructed or regenerated facial nerves in rodents
author: Takeuchi, Osaki, et al.
materials: Seven to thirteen weeks after reconstruction or regeneration surgery, the buccal branch can be reconnected with sufficient physical strength to become physiologically functional [1,2,7]. CMAPs from the vibrissal muscles are then able to be recorded after stimulation of the reconstructed or regenerated nerves [8,9]. A schematic overview of these CMAP recordings is shown in Fig. 1. The materials for the recordings are listed in Table 1. Note that those materials on the list could be replaced with comparable ones from other manufacturers (see Additional information of the Appendix A.). We provide a hands-on manual for CMAP recordings in the CMAPMethods dataset in Mendeley Data (https://doi.org/10.17632/9g5n35fd3f.1) [10].Fig. 1Schematic system overview of a compound muscle action potential (CMAP) recording of vibrissal muscles after stimulation of the buccal branch of facial nerves.A screw-type reference electrode is fixed on the skull and a recording microelectrode is inserted in the whisker pad of an anesthetized rat. Differential potentials between these electrodes are band-pass filtered and amplified with a bio-amplifier and fed to a computer interface. A stimulator delivers TTL signals to trigger data acquisition via the interface. Shortly after beginning the data acquisition process, the stimulator triggers a monopolar square pulse via an isolator to evoke CMAP through the excitation of reconstructed or regenerated facial nerves.Fig. 1Table 1Material list for CMAP recordings. steps.title: Anesthetize for nerve reconstruction
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia with 4 % isoflurane delivered via a nasal mask connected to a Univentor 400 anesthesia unit.

steps.title: Expose facial nerve branches
steps.instruction: Make a left‑side periauricular incision, expose the buccal and marginal mandibular branches of the facial nerve and the parotid gland.

steps.title: Cut marginal mandibular branch
steps.instruction: Transect the marginal mandibular branch with microsurgical scissors and ligate the stump with 7‑0 nylon sutures.

steps.title: Create buccal nerve defect
steps.instruction: Exfoliate the buccal branch from surrounding connective tissue and excise a 7 mm segment to create a defect.

steps.title: Treat nerve defect
steps.instruction: Repair the 7 mm defect either by autologous grafting from the contralateral buccal branch or by inserting a silicone tube filled with type I collagen solution as a nerve conduit.

steps.title: Anesthetize for CMAP recording
steps.instruction: Place the rat in a transparent box, deliver 2–3 % isoflurane until the animal is immobile (including whiskers), then administer urethane intraperitoneally at 1.2 g kg⁻¹ in split doses.

steps.title: Shave animal
steps.instruction: Shave hair on the face and head with a clipper, leaving the whiskers intact for later muscle‑contraction monitoring.

steps.title: Expose buccal nerve for recording
steps.instruction: Under an operating microscope, make a left‑side pre‑auricular incision, expose the buccal branch, stitch the skin with 5‑0 nylon sutures, and exfoliate ~10 mm of free nerve.

steps.title: Mount rat in stereotaxic frame
steps.instruction: Insert accessory ear bars into the external auditory canals, place the upper incisors in the mouthpiece, and pull the mouthpiece anteriorly to secure the skull.

steps.title: Control body temperature
steps.instruction: Place a heater mat under the rat and insert a rectal thermistor probe of a DC temperature controller into the rectum.

steps.title: Place reference electrode
steps.instruction: Expose the skull over the cerebellum, remove periosteum, drill a small hole, and fix a screw‑type reference electrode into the skull using a precision driver.

steps.title: Position stimulus electrode
steps.instruction: Lift the reconstructed/regenerated buccal branch with a hook‑shaped bipolar stimulus electrode, fix it to the stereotaxic apparatus with dental utility wax, and apply a few drops of liquid paraffin or mineral oil to prevent drying.

steps.title: Connect and set stimulus intensity
steps.instruction: Connect the stimulus electrode to an isolator (distal to minus, proximal to plus), deliver test pulses via the stimulator, and adjust the intensity to 2.0 mA using the digital isolator; verify whisker and vibrissal muscle movement after each pulse.

steps.title: Insert recording electrode
steps.instruction: Make a small skin incision on vibrissal rows C and D of the whisker pad, insert a recording microelectrode into the vibrissal muscles, and secure it to a micromanipulator.

steps.title: Connect electrodes to acquisition system
steps.instruction: Connect the reference and recording electrodes to the input box (or pre‑amplifier), short the reference (–) and ground (earth) terminals, and ensure differential signals are band‑pass filtered and amplified by the bio‑amplifier before reaching the computer interface.

steps.title: Start data acquisition
steps.instruction: Press ‘START’ in LabChart software to begin acquisition, then trigger the stimulator to deliver monopolar square pulses via the isolator and record CMAPs.

steps.title: Collect stable trials
steps.instruction: Record at least ten stable CMAP trials; if stability is achieved, stop the stimulator and acquisition software.

steps.title: Save recording file
steps.instruction: Save the acquired data on the PC as a .adicht file (or other LabChart extension).

steps.title: Euthanize animal
steps.instruction: Euthanize the rat with excess isoflurane or perform transcardial perfusion for subsequent anatomical analysis.

steps.title: Export data for analysis
steps.instruction: Export the .adicht file from LabChart as an Igor Pro experiment file (e.g., .pxp).

steps.title: Open data in Igor Pro
steps.instruction: Launch Igor Pro and open the exported .pxp file.

steps.title: Launch CMAPAnalysis panel
steps.instruction: Click ‘CMAP_Preparation’ in the macro menu to open the CMAPControlPanel window.

steps.title: Select and display waves
steps.instruction: In the Data Browser, select the waves to analyze, right‑click and choose ‘Display’ to plot them in a new graph window.

steps.title: Set target graph and source list
steps.instruction: Use the ‘Get’ button in the Target Window group to set the graph as the target window, then use the ‘Get’ button in the Target Wave group to retrieve the list of source waves.

steps.title: Duplicate and baseline‑subtract
steps.instruction: Press ‘Duplicate’ to copy the source waves, then press ‘BaseSub’ to subtract baseline DC shifts.

steps.title: Average duplicated waves
steps.instruction: Press ‘Average’ to compute the mean of the duplicated waves; the averaged waveform appears in the graph window.

steps.title: Place cursors on averaged CMAP
steps.instruction: Place cursor ‘A’ at the onset and cursor ‘B’ at the offset of the averaged CMAP (zero‑crossing points).

steps.title: Set stimulus artifact onset
steps.instruction: Enter the stimulus artifact onset time (e.g., 1 ms) in the edit box on the control panel.

steps.title: Generate summary table
steps.instruction: Click ‘Run’, then ‘Print’ and ‘Edit’ to produce the summary table (TableCMAP) and populate the control‑panel edit boxes.

steps.title: Export summary as CSV
steps.instruction: Press the ‘Save’ button on the control panel, confirm the prompt, and export the summary table as a .csv file.

steps.title: Create publication‑quality graphs
steps.instruction: Use the ‘MGraph1–5’ buttons to format the averaged trace, then export each graph as an .eps file for vector graphics editing.

steps.title: Free‑floating tissue staining
steps.instruction: Perform staining at room temperature in a light‑shielded environment:

substeps.instruction: Incubate tissue in 10 % NRS in PBS‑XCR for 30 min on a shaker.
Incubate in Go anti‑CTB (1:10 000 dilution in PBS‑XCR) overnight on a shaker.
Incubate in biotinylated rabbit anti‑Go IgG (1:400 dilution in PBS‑XCR) for 2 h on a shaker.
Incubate in Alexa 633‑conjugated streptavidin (1:400 dilution in PBS‑X) for 2 h on a shaker.

steps.title: Fluorescent Nissl counterstain
steps.instruction: Counterstain the tissue with fluorescent Nissl:

substeps.instruction: Incubate in fluorescent Nissl solution (1:150 dilution, blue) for 40–60 min.
